correctness.rationale: On the unit grid a nonflat cell has both slope-to-secant ratios in [0,lambda] and a flat cell has zero slopes. Each normalized derivative is in the convex hull of 6t(1-t), 3(1-t)^2, 3t^2, and 3(1-2t)^2 when 0<=lambda<=3, so its integral absolute value is one. Minmod along an input line segment is piecewise affine, switching between the two secant inputs and zero. One secant-direction column thus has variation one in its own cell by the same square test, and at most two disjoint, optional neighboring pure Hermite basis terms, each of variation 8 lambda/27 by their single turning points at 1/3 and 2/3. Summing columns and integrating along the line segment proves the global bound, including ties (every continuous piecewise-linear scalar restriction is absolutely continuous). With two knots there are no slopes, with three one adjacent slope can vary, and with four or more both can vary. A perturbation of size 1/4 in the unique smaller positive secant next to secants of size 2 realizes the full number without selector changes, even at lambda=0 or 3. For n>=3, first secants (1,1) force the normalized first-cell derivative to be t[(6-2 lambda)+(3 lambda-6)t]; it is negative just right of zero for lambda>3 and just left of one for lambda<0, giving excess variation. Reviewed check.py and its finite diagnostic scope; no uploaded script was run. This rejection is not a mathematical counterexample.

originality.rationale: The principal exact two-input result is already known at unit scale on a broader domain, and the remaining formula is a mechanical specialization and rescaling of its published proof using the classical [0,3]^2 Hermite slope square. The earlier Resultary minimax proof explicitly gives the step-column decomposition, the exact 8/27 integrals, the homotopy bound and a same-secant extremizer. Replacing the two coefficient ranges [0,1] by [0,lambda] leaves the central integral equal to 1 by Huynh's four-corner criterion, multiplies each off-cell term by lambda, and deleting unavailable neighbors changes their count to min(2,n-2). The same extremizer, retaining only the available adjacent cells, gives sharpness. Thus the all-scale formula is not asserted verbatim by the earlier theorem, but its extra cases introduce no new norm calculation. The sharp one-input endpoint check is elementary slope monotonicity on the axis (0,lambda), also not a surviving original contribution.
